chunks.title: Defining & counting vision loss
chunks.tldr: ICD-10 (WHO) uses presenting VA in the better eye: moderate impairment (<6/18), severe (<6/60), blindness <3/60 or field ≤10° radius (US 'legal blindness' = best-corrected ≤20/200 or field ≤20° diameter). Presenting VA counts uncorrected refractive error, nearly doubling prevalence. Driving: most US states ~20/40 binocular; Canada 6/15 + 120° horizontal field, no central diplopia — doctors must ensure unfit patients don't drive. WHO 2010: 285 million with vision loss, 39 million blind; 82% over 50, ~90% in low/middle-income countries, 64% women; 19 million children (1.4 million irreversibly blind).
chunks.hook: World's #1 cause of vision loss = uncorrected refractive error; #1 cause of blindness = cataract.

cards.a: Presenting VA worse than 3/60 in the better eye (or visual field <10° from fixation).

chunks.title: Global causes: cataract, refraction, glaucoma, trachoma, oncho
chunks.tldr: Developing world: cataract (backlog ~10 million; UV, dehydration from diarrhoea implicated; 10-year delay would halve surgery need), uncorrected refraction (12 million children), glaucoma (open-angle in West Africa; angle closure in China/SE Asia; ~3 million blind; adherence problem), trachoma (blind fell 6 → 1.8 million; azithromycin + SAFE), onchocerciasis (black fly, Volta basin; mass ivermectin success), leprosy (triple therapy), xerophthalmia (5 million kids/yr; vit A supplementation), corneal ulcers. Developed world: AMD, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, plus HSV, RD, vascular, inherited. Children: retinal disease incl. ROP 29%, corneal scarring (vit A, measles/rubella, infection) 21%, congenital 14%; developed — ROP, cataract, retinal dystrophy, CVI, malformations, nystagmus.
chunks.hook: Poor countries go blind from cataract and scars; rich countries from AMD, diabetes and glaucoma.

chunks.title: Preventing injury & infection
chunks.tldr: ~55 million eye injuries/yr; 57% under 30. Work: grinding/drilling projectiles, sharp tools, welding UV, chemicals → guards, goggles (for bystanders too), training; DIY risk. Ask about injury in any unexplained inflammation (occult IOFB). Radiation workers → cataract. Sport (squash, baseball, hockey), corks, BB guns, fireworks → polycarbonate eyewear. UV: pterygium, lid cancers, cataract; eclipse/solar retinopathy — use filters; operating microscope phototoxicity. Infection: organisms that cross intact epithelium — Neisseria, Corynebacterium diphtheriae, Haemophilus aegyptius, Listeria, Shigella, Acanthamoeba. Protect exposed/anaesthetic eyes (CPA surgery, coma). Surgery: povidone-iodine pre-op, intracameral cefuroxime; lid/sac infections treated first. CL: overnight wear ×5 risk; no swimming/hot tubs; spare specs. Developing world: antibiotic ointment after agricultural abrasions prevents ulcers. Neonates: maternal treatment, erythromycin prophylaxis.

cards.q: Name organisms that can penetrate intact corneal epithelium.
cards.a: Neisseria gonorrhoeae/meningitidis, Corynebacterium diphtheriae, Haemophilus aegyptius, Listeria, Shigella (also Acanthamoeba).

chunks.title: Clinic infection control, congenital & genetic prevention
chunks.tldr: EKC outbreaks spread by hands, tonometers, contaminated drops; separate waiting/exam areas cut hospital-acquired adenovirus from 48% to 3%. Pseudomonas once contaminated fluorescein. Tonometer tips: 70% isopropyl alcohol wipe, dry fully (kills HBV, HIV, HSV, adenovirus) — not prions (hypochlorite or disposable tips); non-contact tonometer aerosols. Hand hygiene every patient. Congenital: rubella vaccine; no CMV vaccine (ganciclovir); toxo — cook meat, wash produce, gloves for cat litter/gardening; antenatal treatment from 15 wk reduces transmission (40% risk if primary infection in pregnancy). HSV-2: 50% transmission with active genital lesions at delivery → caesarean; avoid scalp electrodes; disseminated neonatal HSV 75% mortality. Genetic: counselling, prenatal diagnosis; RB at-risk kids examined 6-monthly to 5–6 y unless gene-negative.
chunks.hook: Alcohol wipe the tonometer — and let it dry, or you'll make an abrasion.

cards.q: How should applanation tonometer tips be disinfected between patients?
cards.a: Wipe with 70% isopropyl alcohol and allow to dry completely (or use disposable tips); prions need hypochlorite.

chunks.title: Systemic disease, drugs & screening
chunks.tldr: Diabetic retinopathy: leading cause of blindness age 20–64 in developed world; ~40% of diabetics; type 1 none for ≥3 y, type 2 up to 20% at diagnosis → annual dilated photos, more in pregnancy; control glucose/BP/lipids/renal. Vitamin A deficiency: poverty, malabsorption, bowel/bariatric surgery, faddy diets, alcoholism → night blindness, Bitot spots; IM vitamin A, prophylaxis. Drugs: topical steroids (infection, HSV, glaucoma, PSC), never home anaesthetic drops, preservative toxicity; systemic drugs (SJS, angle closure, optic neuropathy, retinopathy) → drug history. Screening: POAG (0.1% at 40s → 5% >75; OHT 10× commoner) — annual IOP + disc in first-degree relatives, everyone >50 every 3–5 y; DR; ROP (<30 wk, ≤1500 g, oxygen); amblyopia (neonatal red reflex, cover test, refer strabismus >3 months, preschool VA, photoscreening); JIA uveitis 6-monthly (oligoarticular ANA+). Urgent-symptom conditions: keratitis, AACG, wet AMD, RD, GCA.
chunks.hook: Screen what is silent but treatable: glaucoma, diabetes, ROP, amblyopia, JIA.

cards.q: Which eye conditions merit routine screening because they are silent but treatable?
cards.a: Primary open-angle glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, ROP, amblyopia, JIA-associated uveitis.
